thread:
elaine: Quick sync — proposing a 'scheduled degradation' opt-in for Reserved Pools. Customers can pre-book windows where we intentionally reduce throughput (e.g., 30–60%) in exchange for a pricing credit. Goal: give predictable cost-saving for workloads that can tolerate lower capacity (nightly ETL, batch embeddings). Thoughts?

mike: curious — is this a static schedule per-tenant or dynamic policy? how does autoscale interact?

elaine: initial MVP = static schedule per-tenant + timezone support. Autoscale still applies but with a capped headroom during the window.

sara: +1 for timezone support. Ops concern: we need an escape hatch if latency SLOs break during the window. Otherwise oncall will get paged nonstop.

jason: product note — contract/legal needs clear language: "scheduled degradation" and guaranteed fallback path. Also want launch criteria: 3 customers signed to pilot, runbook, and billing calc for credits.

adrian: implementation sketch: represent each opt-in window as a hot-schedule object on the admission controller. During window, admission controller enforces a lower token-bucket rate and reduces batch size hints for runtime. Fallback route -> route traffic to hosted-compatible model variant or spill to burst pool.

hana: we already had a pilot ask from Acme Analytics: they'd take 40% sustained throughput drop nightly 01:00–05:00 local time if they get ~25% monthly credit.

mike: how do we prevent accidental double-penalties? e.g., tenant in scheduled window but also hits preemption on a high-priority pool. Need deterministic conflict resolution rules.

adrian: propose priority resolution: 1) safety escape (if latency > SLO for X min) 2) emergency preempt (oncall override) 3) scheduled degradation. Basically scheduled is the lowest priority overrideable by safety signals.

sara: runbook stub ideas — thresholds: p95 latency > 2x SLO for 3m -> auto-fallback; error-rate spike > 5% for 5m -> notify + fallback; manual abort with one-click in Console.

jason: UI needs — Console toggle to opt-in, calendar view of windows, projected credits preview, opt-in audit trail + contract checkbox. Also API: POST /reserved_pools/{id}/degradation_windows.

elaine: here's a quick config example for the API we talked about:

```
POST /api/v1/reserved_pools/123/degradation_windows
{
  "start": "2026-04-01T01:00:00-07:00",
  "end":   "2026-04-01T05:00:00-07:00",
  "throughput_multiplier": 0.6,
  "discount_pct": 25,
  "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles",
  "safety_triggers": {"p95_latency_ms": 2000, "error_rate_pct": 5}
}
```

mike: that helps. runtime question — will KV cache behaviour change? if we throttle we may evict more often, causing tail latency. need to model this for SLA impact.

adrian: agree. we'll add a 'cache_weight' hint to the window so runtime can prefer keeping short-lived sessions cached. Also run simulation to estimate tail bumps.

hana: billing: is discount applied pro-rata for the window or full-day credit? Acme prefers pro-rata per-window credits added to monthly invoice.

jason: prefer pro-rata per-window to keep it simple and transparent. Also add opt-out clause for unexpected production regressions within pilot.

elaine: launch checklist (proposed):
- pilot sign-ups: 3 enterprise customers (sales + solutions)
- runbook + automated escape hatch implemented
- Console + API MVP for scheduling and audit
- billing flow for per-window credits
- two-week internal canary + 1-week customer pilot

sara: add: oncall playbook + pager thresholds, and test drill to trigger auto-fallback.

mike: engineering asks: ETA for admission change + API surface? estimate 3 sprint for admission/controller + 2 sprint for Console + 1 sprint for billing glue. depends on prioritization.

elaine: noted. action items: @adrian to draft RFC with admission semantics and safety triggers; @mike to run early simulation for cache/latency; @jason to draft pilot contract language; @sara to draft runbook and drill steps; @hana to secure initial pilot lead (Acme). ops-bot: create tickets for each?

ops-bot: Created ticket IRIS-4723 (admission RFC), IRIS-4724 (console scheduling UI), IRIS-4725 (billing credits), IRIS-4726 (runbook + drills).

elaine: thanks — I'll sync with Sales to firm up pilot customers and follow up next Tue. If anyone has objections to priority, flag now. :thumbsup:
